text:
maya (support): Hey team — customer AcmeChat is hitting a sudden p95 spike and 5xxs on our score-sort endpoint (/v1/score-sort). They started at ~21:50 UTC, spike at ~22:13. Errors: lots of 502s and gateway timeouts. Sample request id: req_0a1b2c3d. Customer says this happens only under bursty rerank batches (they send 400 qps in short bursts).

ian (eng-oncall): Thanks — can you paste the raw payload shape and any request-ids + client-side retry config? Also is this hosted or Dedicated?

maya (support): Hosted. Payload is basically an array of candidates (~120 items) + user context. They said client retries on 500/502 with exponential backoff starting at 30ms and no jitter. Example curl they sent:

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/score-sort \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"query":"...","candidates":["...","...", ... 120 items]}'
```

Response times before spike: p95 ~120ms. During spike p95 jumped to 3.2s and many 502s.

rachel (eng-runtime): Two quick hypotheses: 1) large candidate lists causing oversized batches + KV cache thrash; 2) client retry pattern producing retry storm that overwhelms gateway and worker pool. Do we have gateway request queue depth / worker kills?

chen (eng-infra): Pulling logs now. I see a tight cluster of 502s from the gateway at 22:12:58. Backend worker pool (score-sort-v2) shows ephemeral CPU saturation + container restarts for several pods between 22:13:00–22:13:30. Reason: worker PID OOM in several instances (OOMKilled). Also connection backlog in envoy increased. Metrics: worker concurrency spiked from 50 -> 240 in ~30s. Link to graph (internal): https://grafana.internal/shot/abc123 (internal).

sam (cs): Customer confirms client-side retry interval is aggressive and no jitter. They also admitted they batch requests from multiple users into one large rerank call to save tokens.

ian (eng-oncall): That explains it — big batch + tight retries = thundering herd. Short term: can we flip gateway circuit breaker to fast-fail on high queue depth and return 429 to callers so they back off? Also increase gateway timeout to 10s and add request-level backpressure on the model pool.

rachel (eng-runtime): Agreed. Immediate actions I can take:
- Reduce default max batch size for score-sort-v2 from 128 -> 64 for the cluster serving AcmeChat traffic.
- Enable per-model queue_circuit with threshold 200ms queueing latency -> return 429.
- Add KV cache pre-warm for common prefixes (helps long candidate lists).

ian (eng-oncall): Chen — can infra spin up a temporary extra replica set for that model so we have more headroom while we tune?

chen (eng-infra): Yep. Spawning +4 replicas and bumping pod memory limit from 8G -> 12G for the next 2 hours. Also adding an envoy limit on concurrent downstream connections per route to 100 to stop unlimited fanout.

ops-bot: [deploy] Started rolling update on score-sort-v2 replicas. CI run id: 8791.

maya (support): I asked customer to stop aggressive retries and to add jitter; they applied a soft cap on candidates per request to 64 as a temporary workaround.

sam (cs): Customer reports errors dropped immediately after they capped candidate count and reduced retry aggressiveness. They're still seeing slightly elevated latencies but no 502 spike.

rachel (eng-runtime): Follow-ups:
- We'll keep the reduced batch size and monitor p95 for 2 hours.
- Backport a small change to gateway to return 429 earlier when queue depth > 150.
- Add an advisory in support KB about client retry jitter and recommended client-side backoff for large batch rerank.

ian (eng-oncall): Helpful debug tip for future: capture `X-Req-ID`, `route`, and `pool-metrics` (queue length, inflight) at time of 5xx. If you see synchronized retries from clients, treat it as a retry storm and prioritize queue/circuit mitigations.

chen (eng-infra): Postmortem checklist items:
- Confirm OOM root cause (maybe memory leak under specific candidate size).
- Evaluate autoscaler thresholds for burst scenarios.
- Add an alert for sudden worker restarts tied to queue depth.

maya (support): Customer confirmed after fix: requests stable, no 502s for 45 minutes. Closing the escalation unless we see recurrence. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

ian (eng-oncall): Nice work. I'll leave a short incident note in /incidents and assign follow-ups to infra/runtime.

sam (cs): I'll send the KB update and a recommended client config snippet to the customer (showing exponential backoff + jitter + 64 candidate cap).

rachel (eng-runtime): One more note: we should consider adding server-side soft-fail (partial-sort) so very large lists can return a best-effort result instead of tying up full ranker resources. Filed a ticket: RT-4821.

maya (support): Closing thread — marking resolved with customer ack.
